name: Double Chicken Please
take: Cocktails on tap and a hot honey chicken sandwich up front; the Back Room is the reservation you make when you want the full production.
theCatch: The Front Room is walk-in and fills fast after 8; Back Room tables go on Resy a week out.
notes: Two rooms on Allen between Delancey and Rivington: a walk-in Front Room with around a dozen numbered cocktails on tap plus fried chicken sandwiches and chicken liver mousse, and a reserved Back Room with pricier drinks and a more ambitious menu. Has placed high on the World's 50 Best Bars list. Music and crowd pick up later in the evening.

name: Tigre
take: Gold walls, ice-cold martinis, and a fully seated room from the Maison Premiere people; the LES bar for a night when you want to feel like an adult.
theCatch: Book on Resy; walk-in seats are scarce and reservations run on a 90-minute clock.
notes: Seated cocktail lounge between Essex and Ludlow from Premiere Enterprises (Maison Premiere), behind an unmarked door, with gold walls, mirrored bathrooms, and white-jacketed staff. Hours Sun-Mon 5pm-midnight, Tue-Wed 5pm-1am, Thu-Sat 5pm-2am. Reservations via Resy with limited walk-in seating; no standing room; 1.5-hour limit.

name: Little Big
take: Ex-Double Chicken Please bartenders, a shaded backyard, and drinks that borrow from Eastern Europe and the Caribbean; the afternoon-into-evening bar on Clinton.
theCatch: The inside is tiny and the patio shuts at 10, so come early and plan to sit outside.
notes: Newer cocktail bar between Stanton and Rivington opened by former Double Chicken Please bartenders. Small interior; the draw is a covered, tropical-leaning backyard. Small plates such as roast pork between potato pancakes and a starfruit salad; drinks include a tequila milk punch. Hours Mon-Thu 5-11pm, Fri-Sat 4pm-midnight, Sun 4-10pm; patio closes at 10pm.

name: Copper & Oak
take: A library of 600 bottles and a bartender who will find you the Japanese whisky you didn't know you wanted; quiet, serious, and very small.
theCatch: It hits capacity most nights and flashes a 'we are full' sign; a party of two after 7 is the safe bet.
notes: Whiskey bar between Rivington and Stanton from Flavien Desoblin of Brandy Library, with backlit shelves holding roughly 600 bottles and a deep Japanese selection poured in 1 and 2 oz measures; average pour around $18. Time Out lists hours as Tue-Sat 5pm-1am and Sun 2-10pm, closed Monday; confirm before going.

name: Parkside Lounge
address: 317 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002
take: Christmas lights, a pool table, a back room with a stage, and a 4am close; the LES dive that has outlasted every trend on both sides of Houston.
theCatch: Bring a physical ID, a phone photo won't get you in; weeknights are calm and weekends fill without turning rowdy.
notes: Old-school dive at Houston and Attorney with pool, TVs for games, Wednesday trivia, and a back-room stage that hosts bands, drag, and dance parties. Opens 4pm Mon-Thu and 3pm Fri-Sun and stays open until 4am nightly. Some outdoor seating. Strict on real ID.

name: 169 Bar
take: A leopard-print pool table, a fish tank, dumplings at 3am, and drinks that still cost what drinks should; the Two Bridges dive worth the walk south.
theCatch: Happy hour runs 2 to 7:30 every day; weekends get chaotic after midnight, so go early if you want the pool table.
notes: Dive on East Broadway between Jefferson and Rutgers in a bar space dating to 1916, with neon, Christmas lights, a leopard-print pool table, and a kitchen open to 4am serving dumplings, empanadas, and oysters. Open daily 2pm-4am; happy hour 2-7:30pm with discounted drinks and $3 oysters. Weekend DJs playing soul and disco; some covered outdoor seating.

name: Welcome to the Johnsons
take: Wood paneling, bowling trophies, and $3 cans in a bar built to look like somebody's 1970s rec room; the cheap-drinks answer on Rivington.
theCatch: The back room with the pool table is the seat to grab; the summer margaritas are stronger than they taste.
notes: Themed dive open since 1999 between Essex and Norfolk, decorated like a suburban basement with VHS tapes, black-light posters, family photos, and vintage furniture spread across several small rooms. PBR around $3, seasonal margaritas in summer, pool table in the back room. Occasional live music. Crowd mixes locals and younger LES regulars.

name: Sadie's Ward
take: The old Whiskey Ward under a new name and its former bar manager, with pool tables, a long whiskey shelf, and a 4am close seven nights a week.
theCatch: Pool tables get claimed early on weekends; on weeknights it's a regulars' room where you can actually play.
notes: Opened January 2024 in the Whiskey Ward space between Rivington and Delancey after that bar's roughly 24-year run; owner Stephanie Watkins was the Whiskey Ward's bar manager. Whiskey-focused, pool tables, trivia nights listed with the NYC Trivia League. Hours Mon-Fri 5pm-4am, Sat-Sun noon-4am. Named for 1860s LES figure Sadie Farrell.

name: The Ten Bells
take: A dark wraparound bar, natural wine by the generous glass, and dollar oysters until 7; the wine bar that was here long before the neighborhood got a nickname.
theCatch: Get there before 7 for the oysters; after that it's standing room and communal tables, so put a name in on Resy.
notes: Natural wine bar open since 2008 on Broome between Orchard and Ludlow. Spanish-leaning tapas around $10, many bottles under $40, $1 oysters daily until 7pm. Wraparound bar, high-tops, and communal tables. Hours Mon-Wed 5pm-midnight, Thu-Fri 5pm-1am, Sat 3pm-1am, Sun 3-11pm. Reservations via Resy.

name: Le Dive
take: A French tabac on the Dimes Square corner where the wine is natural, the plaza is packed, and everyone is watching everyone; come for the sidewalk.
theCatch: Walk-in waits can hit an hour on weekends; the outdoor plaza is the whole point, so it's a different bar in January.
notes: French tabac-styled natural wine bar at Canal and Orchard, the center of Dimes Square. Small interior with a handful of stools and one row of tables, plus a large outdoor plaza. Orange wine by the glass around $17; snacks like steak tartare, burrata, and smoked salmon. The Infatuation reported no reservations and hour-long waits; the venue site now lists reservations for the LES location and a second location in the West Village.

name: Loreley Beer Garden
take: A Cologne-style beer hall with a big heated garden out back and long tables built for eight; the answer to 'where can all of us sit outside.'
theCatch: The garden closes at 10:45 and tables run on a two-hour clock; reserve ahead, and after 9 it's indoor only.
notes: German biergarten on Rivington between Bowery and Chrystie, modeled on a Cologne brauhaus, with a large heated outdoor garden, an indoor hall, and a party room for 20-50. Hours Mon-Tue 5pm-midnight, Wed-Thu 5pm-1am, Fri-Sat noon-4am, Sun noon-midnight; garden closes 10:45pm. Reservations up to 15 people, 1.5-2 hour limits, no standing room; weekend brunch noon-4pm.

name: Mr. Purple
address: 180 Orchard St, 15th Fl, New York, NY 10002
take: Fifteen floors up with two terraces, a view from Midtown to the bridges, and a crowd that dressed for the photo; the LES rooftop, for better and worse.
theCatch: Lines form fast around sunset, especially on weekends; weekday happy hour from 4 to 7 is the easy way in.
notes: Rooftop bar on the 15th floor of Hotel Indigo between Stanton and Houston, with two terraces and an indoor lounge; the pool is for hotel guests only. Hours Mon-Wed 4pm-2am, Thu 4pm-3am, Fri 4pm-4am, Sat-Sun from 2pm. Happy hour Mon-Fri 4-7pm with $11 cocktails and wine and $6 bites. DJs; smart-casual door policy.

name: Hair of the Dog
take: Projectors, big screens, beer pong, and half-off everything until 7 on weekdays; the LES sports bar that doesn't pretend to be anything else.
theCatch: Skews young and loud on game days and weekend nights; weekday afternoons are the calm, cheap version.
notes: Sports bar on Orchard between Stanton and Houston with multiple screens and projectors, beer pong, bar food, and a college-heavy crowd. Open from noon daily; until 1am Sun-Wed, 3am Thu, 4am Fri-Sat. Weekday happy hour noon-7pm with all drinks half off and $3 sliders; nightly specials after 7pm and a $35 boozy brunch on weekends.

name: Home Sweet Home
take: Taxidermy, a disco ball, and a basement full of people actually dancing to records; the cheap late-night move once the cocktail bars have closed.
theCatch: Friday's 50s-and-60s party runs 10:30 to 4 and packs the room; a stairway down is the only sign it exists.
notes: Subterranean bar on Chrystie between Delancey and Broome, open since 2006, with a small dance floor under a disco ball, taxidermy throughout, and DJs and live music on weekends from 10pm to close. Hours Mon-Sat 6pm-4am, Sun 8pm-4am; happy hour weekdays until 8:30pm. Drafts, bottles, frozen drinks, and rotating cocktails, all inexpensive.

name: Lullaby
take: A low-ceilinged basement under a sushi bar where the cocktails are real, the playlist is somebody's record collection, and the couches turn into a dance floor by 11.
theCatch: It's small and the couches go early; arrive before 10 on weekends if you want to sit.
notes: Basement cocktail bar below Sake Bar Yopparai on Rivington between Suffolk and Clinton, opened 2022. Couches, low ceilings, frozen Dole Whip cocktails and a Negroni Whip, and a crate-digger playlist; people dance though there's no formal floor. Time Out lists cocktails under $15 and beers up to $7. Not hidden and not a speakeasy despite the location.

name: Wildair
take: Natural wine, a beef tartare people cross the city for, and a room full of good haircuts; the LES dinner that flows straight into a bar.
theCatch: Walk-ins usually land a bar seat on weeknights; order the house chilled red and let the server pick the rest.
notes: Wine-forward small-plates restaurant on Orchard between Rivington and Stanton, opened 2015 as the casual sibling of Contra (now closed). Seasonal shareable plates mostly under $35, a rotating beef tartare, fried stuffed olives, and a natural wine list with a house chilled red bottled for them in Anjou. Takes reservations; walk-ins usually seated at the bar or a table most nights.

name: Freemans
take: Down a dead-end alley, antlers on the walls, and roast chicken and pork chops that haven't needed to change since 2004; dinner that makes visitors feel like insiders.
theCatch: Reservations open 14 days out for up to eight; nine or more need the private room, and Banzarbar upstairs is the nightcap.
notes: Rustic American tavern at the end of Freeman Alley off Rivington between Bowery and Chrystie, open since 2004, styled like a colonial tavern with taxidermy and vintage back-bar fittings. Dinner Sun-Mon 5-10pm, Tue-Sat 5-11pm, plus weekday lunch and weekend brunch. Cocktails around $20-21. Reservations for 1-8 via Resy up to 14 days ahead with some walk-in seating held; groups of 9+ go to private rooms. Banzarbar is a roughly 20-seat cocktail bar upstairs.

name: Wu's Wonton King
take: Big round tables, seafood tanks, roast duck, and a wonton soup the size of a punch bowl; the BYOB group dinner that costs less than the bar after.
theCatch: Bring your own bottles; call ahead for the whole suckling pig, and 169 Bar is a few doors down when you're done.
notes: Cantonese restaurant on East Broadway between Jefferson and Rutgers, open since 2016, with big round tables, live seafood tanks, roast meats, whole fried crab, and a family-style wonton soup; BYOB. Whole suckling pig must be ordered in advance. In June 2026 a minority partner left to open his own place; The Lo-Down reports the owner, name, kitchen team, and menu are unchanged.

name: Scarr's Pizza
take: The slice the neighborhood argues is the best, now with a back room for whole pies and arcade games; dinner for people saving their money for the bar.
theCatch: There is a line, always; ask for the back and order a whole pie instead of fighting for a counter slice.
notes: Retro slice shop that moved from 22 Orchard to a larger room at 35 Orchard between Canal and Hester, with counter slices up front and a back dining area for whole pies plus arcade games. Thin New York slices, a Sicilian, and pepperoni-jalapeno. Hours Sun-Wed 11:30am-11pm, Thu to midnight, Fri-Sat to 2am. Lines are routine; the site lists OpenTable reservations.

name: Bacaro
take: A brick-vaulted Venetian cellar lit by candles, with cicchetti and squid-ink spaghetti on long wooden tables; the Dimes Square dinner that was here before Dimes Square.
theCatch: Ask for downstairs and book ahead; it gets loud near the bar, and it's closed Mondays.
notes: Venetian restaurant on Division between Orchard and Ludlow, open since 2007, with a ground floor and a candlelit brick cellar of long wooden tables and benches. Cicchetti, spaghetti nero, duck cavatelli; pastas around $21-22, mains $20-32. Hours Tue-Sat 5pm-midnight, Sun 5-10pm, closed Monday. Gratuity included for parties of six or more; reviewers note noise near the bar.
